keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; Cliopatria has no row for the Bishopric of Courland (its Livonian Conference row of 1422-1561 covers Old Livonia as a whole). The page names 'Pilten' as a castle and 'Piltene' as the capital, says the bishopric 'consisted of three separate enclaves' and ruled the island of Runö (Ruhnu) from at least 1341; the Livonian Confederation page gives 4,500 km2. The page is silent on boundaries, so the Ventspils area is the researcher's reading, one of the three enclaves at best.

ledger.note: 1234: the bishopric is established. Infobox 'Established: 11 February 1234'; the timeline has 'September 1234' but also says it was 'formally declared on 11 February 1232', and the body names the Dominican friar Engelbert as the first bishop in 1234; the page does not resolve this. The page is silent on what land the bishop held before the 1253 division, so the Pilten area is drawn at confidence 1.

region.text: Pilten (Piltene), the bishopric's capital, which the researcher reads as the Ventspils area; the page gives no boundary and names three separate enclaves

ledger.note: 1253: Courland is divided. 'The territory of Courland was divided' in 1253 between the bishopric and the Livonian branch of the Teutonic Order; the page names no districts, so the Pilten area stands for the bishop's share (4,500 km2 on the Livonian Confederation page, at the Confederation's date). The curonians dossier carries the Curonian partition of 1266 'between the Livonian Order and the Archbishop of Riga' on the Curonians page: the pages disagree on who shared Courland with the Order.

ledger.note: 1559-1560: the bishopric is sold. The body says Bishop Johann V von Münchhausen 'sold his lands to King Frederick II of Denmark' in 1559; the timeline gives 20 May 1560 for the sale. The Livonian War page says Magnus bought the Bishopric of Courland without his brother's consent and gives no date. 20 May 1560 is used; the infobox gives 'Disestablished: 20 April 1562' with no explanation on the page.

ledger.note: 1560: the bishopric's rule ends with the sale. Magnus later spent his last six years at Pilten and died there as a pensioner of the Polish crown; he 'promised to transfer it to the Duchy of Courland' and Wilhelm Kettler later regained the district; sold by Denmark to Poland-Lithuania on 20 April 1585 (timeline).

certainty.note: Three enclaves on the page, none with a boundary; only the area (4,500 km2) and the capital are given.

notes: Ecclesiastical principality of Terra Mariana. The capital Piltene is not in the gazetteer, so capitals is empty; the bishop's island of Runö (Ruhnu) is not drawn (the Saare county cannot be cut to one island). The Livonian Confederation page gives the area 4,500 km2 at the Confederation's date. The page's own dates for the end disagree (1559 sale, 20 May 1560 timeline, 20 April 1562 infobox, 20 April 1585 sale by Denmark to Poland-Lithuania); the dossier follows the sale in 1560 and does not carry the Danish period 1560-1585 (a counterpart without a dossier). Pilten later belonged to the Duchy of Courland and Semigallia after the Kettlers regained it (page, no year). Review eu-14-x (2026-10-31): the found event lowered to confidence 1, as its own note says (the page is silent on the bishop's land before the 1253 division).
